blocks.text:
Breakfast.

In the afternoon, take a sightseeing tour of Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire, where pre-Columbian heritage and Spanish colonial architecture sit side by side.

The tour begins at Qorikancha, the Temple of the Sun and one of the Inca Empire's most important religious centres. Major ceremonies honouring the sun took place here, including celebrations of the winter solstice.

Then head out of the city to visit four archaeological sites around Cusco:

Sacsayhuamán is a vast complex of massive stone walls, towers and terraces. Its huge stone blocks fit together with remarkable precision, a testament to the skill of the builders.

Q'enqo is an enigmatic ritual complex with passageways, niches and ceremonial spaces cut into the rock.

Puka Pukara, or the Red Fortress, is an ancient fortified complex believed to have served defensive and administrative functions.

Tambomachay is an archaeological site associated with water worship. Its stone channels, terraces and carefully directed streams show the skill of Inca engineers.

A visit to Cusco Cathedral, one of the city's architectural highlights, which houses an extensive collection of religious art. The visit lasts about 40 minutes and costs USD 30 per person. It takes place before the main sightseeing tour.
Overnight at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a comparable hotel in the same category.
